question: How does modification with CuCl2 and ZnCl2 affect structural properties and adsorption performance of 13X zeolites?
answer: Modification with CuCl₂ and ZnCl₂ alters the structural and adsorption properties of 13X zeolites differently. CuCl₂ disperses as a monolayer or submonolayer on 13X, preserving its crystal structure while significantly enhancing phosphine (PH₃) adsorption capacity across a broad temperature range (-15 to 50 °C) via instantaneous adsorption and reaction. In contrast, ZnCl₂ loading disrupts the zeolite structure, relying primarily on physical adsorption, which performs optimally only at lower temperatures. While Zn-13X and unmodified 13X can be regenerated via N₂ purging, Cu-13X exhibits slower degradation in adsorption cycles due to weakly bound PH₃ in outer layers. Cu-13X demonstrates superior static adsorption capacity compared to Zn-13X and unmodified 13X.

### Task 1: Summarize the Purpose of the Paper
The purpose of this paper is to evaluate the performance of ZnCl₂- and CuCl₂-modified 13X zeolites (Zn-13X and Cu-13X) as adsorbents for removing trace amounts of phosphine (PH₃) from hydrogen gas in chemical vapor deposition (CVD) processes, which is critical for maintaining the high purity required in silicon-based semiconductor and photovoltaic applications. The study investigates the adsorption capacities, breakthrough times, and adsorption mechanisms of the modified zeolites at varying temperatures, using techniques such as X-ray diffraction and surface analysis.
